reason: Eacarunculate means without a caruncle, so caruncle absent is right.
Scarcely abundant means few or rare, which fits decreased amount.
Cannelé is French for fluted or grooved, which is furrowed.
Densiflorous means densely flowered, which is a dense arrangement or number of flowers. Condensed loses the flowers.
Ecaliculate means without an epicalyx.
Evase (évasé) means flared, widening outward.
Narrow-sinused means the sinuses are narrow, not the whole part. Decreased width would land on the wrong bearer. The rule needs a sinus bearer.
Pubescent-velvety means hairy with velvety hairs, which is velutinous.
Without claw is not clawed, and FLOPO_0991169 is clawed.
French sarmenteux means with long, flexible, climbing stems, which is climbing.
Acumen is the acuminate tip, so without acumen is not acuminate.
Composite is ambiguous. It can mean compound, as in a compound leaf, or Asteraceae-type. It does not reliably mean a capitulum is present, and the rule would attach one to any part.
Splashed means irregularly blotched, which is mottled.
Thin-valved means the valves are thin. The rule drops the valve and would apply decreased thickness to the whole fruit.
Several-seriate means in several rows, which is multiseriate.
Frilly means ruffled or finely wavy, which is crisped.
Not aculeate means without prickles, so not spiny.
A semisuperior ovary is the same as a half-inferior one.
A bristle-terminated part ends in a bristle or seta. That is not the same as having an awn, and the rule leaves out which part carries it.
Decorated means ornamented.
Glandular dots matches the definition of gland-dotted.
Midnerved means having a midrib. Leaf midvein is only right for leaves. Sepals, bracts and other parts need their own midvein.
Not root-sprouting means no suckers arise from the roots, which is root-borne shoot system absent.
Retrorsely barbed means barbs pointing backward, which matches the definition of barbed.
Spirally ranked means arranged in a spiral.
Tailless means without a tail, so not caudate.
Thyrses describes a thyrse-type inflorescence, which is thyrse-like. The plural form could also be read as an entity, so confidence is modest.
Wide-ovate means broadly ovate, which is a kind of ovate. The width is lost, but ovate is a valid parent class.
Without abaxial keel means the keel on the lower surface is missing. Not keel-shaped drops the abaxial keel as the bearer. Keel (carina) absent would be better.
Without tubers is tuber absent.
Dichasiate means arranged in dichasia, and a dichasium is a cyme. PO lists dichasium as a synonym.
Flower-bearing means it carries flowers, so flower present.
Armed means bearing spines, prickles or thorns, so not armed is not spiny.
Ladderlike is scalariform, so the negation is right.
Prolate means elongated. Short-ellipsoid means a short ellipsoid, nearly rounded, so it is not prolate. An ellipsoid class would fit better.
Abruptly expanded is dilated. The abruptness is lost, but the main meaning stays.
Granular-puberulent means finely hairy and also granular. Puberulous loses the granular texture.
Helmet-like means hooded, which is cucullate.
Rod-like is a listed synonym of cylindrical.
Saccate-dilated means pouch-like swollen, which is saccate.
Shrublike means shrubby in habit, which matches frutescent habit.
Without ridges is not ridged.
Brilliant means shining, which is glistening. It can also describe a bright colour, so confidence is modest.
Conjoined means joined together, which is connate.
Glandular-spotted means marked with gland dots.
Not setose is the negation of setose.
Not spongy is the negation of spongy.
A pipe-like calyx is a tube, which is tubular, and the rule is already limited to the calyx.
Puce is a dark purplish brown-red, close to dark purplish red.
Sanguineous means blood-red, which is deep red.
